test_title: PYST 46 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 29 Nov, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P. A large-scale migration was triggered in 1848 by the discovery of gold in California.

Q. Prospectors from all over the world were drawn to the promise of immediate fortune.

R. Few of the "Forty-Niners" did become wealthy.

S. Towns and communities in the American West proliferated as a result of this migration.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph follows a logical narrative arc: establishing a historical catalyst, explaining the motivation for human movement, describing the resulting societal growth, and concluding with the reality of the outcome.
 
• **Sentence P is the first sentence** as it introduces the specific event and time period that serves as the foundation for the entire paragraph:
 
 
• "A large-scale migration was triggered in 1848 by the discovery of gold in California."
 
 
 
• **Sentence Q follows** by identifying the people involved and their motivation for participating in this migration:
 
 
• "Prospectors from all over the world were drawn to the promise of immediate fortune."
 
 
 
• **Sentence S is the third sentence** as it describes the broader geographical and structural impact that this massive influx of people had on the region:
 
 
• "Towns and communities in the American West proliferated as a result of this migration."
 
 
 
• **Sentence R is the fourth sentence** because it provides a concluding observation or "reality check" regarding the individuals mentioned earlier in the text:
 
 
• "Few of the 'Forty-Niners' did become wealthy."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **PQSR**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"A large-scale migration was triggered in 1848 by the discovery of gold in California. Prospectors from all over the world were drawn to the promise of immediate fortune. Towns and communities in the American West proliferated as a result of this migration. Few of the 'Forty-Niners' did become wealthy."
